note: Pinned revisions of the sibling repositories sb3-creator's cross-repo gates consume. CI checks these exact commits out beside the repo (.github/workflows/ci.yml) so the gates RUN rather than skip; test/helpers/siblings.mjs turns an absent sibling into a failure when CI=true. Update a pin deliberately, in its own commit, with the suite green against it. `rev` MUST be the FULL 40-character SHA: actions/checkout only recognises a full SHA as a commit, and turns anything shorter into `git fetch origin +refs/heads/<ref>*` — a branch glob that matches nothing. An abbreviated pin here took every CI run on main down at the checkout step, before lint, tests, the mutation prover or the build ran at all. gate-integrity asserts the length; `revShort` exists only for prose.

bw-board.why: the device/board simulator the gallery e2e and physics gates drive. BUMPED 2026-09-21 from 7b7f3b50 to master's tip 4ae99bea, 1,409 commits, and the reason is that the APP HAD ALREADY MOVED: brickwright-lite ships this engine, so every number these gates certified was a number no learner could see. The range is dominated by one model change — an LED is solved on its diode junction instead of clamped at a knee — and that is re-derived rather than absorbed. MEASURED: 23 of 7,451 tests failed at this pin before the re-derivation, in four families. (1) Seventeen assert-block voltages, every LED or diode forward drop, all LOWER by 0.19-0.25 V (21-resistor-led 2.13 -> 1.9391, 40-led-color-mix blue 3.25 -> 3.0048, 28-diode-polarity 2.79 -> 2.5434). The new figure is the better one: a '2.0 V' red LED is quoted at its rated 20 mA, and these benches run it near 3-14 mA, where it really does sit lower. (2) Twenty prose quantities, including worked arithmetic that had to stay self-consistent — 23-voltage-regulator's whole power budget, pc13-direct-diode's conclusion INVERTED (the hand calculation with textbook drops used to land 10 % high and now lands 4 % low, because the junctions sit below their quoted figures at this current rather than above), pc07 and 41-pot-as-dimmer's dimmer sweeps, pico01-blink's measured branch. (3) The V_CE(sat) claims in four transistor lessons: the engine now reports 0.078 V where it reported about 0.2 V, and the lessons say so while keeping the rule of thumb as prose. (4) Two gate repairs that are NOT data: device-branch-agreement compared two readings of the same current at 1e-6, which only held because a clamped diode came out of one linear solve; a Newton-solved junction leaves a residual, measured at 8.19e-5 worst case against the 1.55e4 relative difference of the defect that gate exists to catch (43 A through a 2.772 mA resistor), so the threshold is now 1e-3 — a separation between two measured numbers. And nmos.vth/nmos.k became unprobeable because bw-board stopped LEAKING through an off MOSFET: pc39-nmos-switch's drain sat at 3.0245 V with its gate switch open at the old pin and sits at 4.9950 V now, so a perturbation that used to show through the leak shows nothing. Both are recorded as blind spots with the closed-switch measurement (vth 2 -> 1.3243 V, vth 8.4 -> 4.9950 V) that names the fix. The overcurrent e2e provenance is re-stamped, not re-pointed: 46-port-overcurrent now carries 18.286 mA per branch against 17.143, and its 20 mA margin narrowed to 1.7 mA. bw-board master CI is green on 4ae99bea. PRIOR: the device/board simulator the gallery e2e and physics gates drive. BUMPED 2026-09-08 from 338ac5d to master's tip 7b7f3b5, and the bump is FORCED by DEVICE REGISTRATION that postdates the previous pin: src/devices/retro-dips.js registers the Intel 8086 CPU and 8255 PPI (registerDevice('i8086', ...) at retro-dips.js:200 and registerDevice('i8255', ...) at :202). At 338ac5d those chips' FILES existed (src/i8255.js, i8086-adapter.js, i8086-extract.js) but the DEVICES were not registered — and that is the distinction that decides the failure. bw-circuit-ui's engineKindFor() keeps a PASSTHROUGH_KINDS kind only if the engine resolves a device model for it (eng.getDevice(kind)); otherwise it collapses to a generic 'mcu'. So the incoming i8086-blink example's cpu86 (kind i8086) loaded as a generic 40-pin MCU, and every address-bus wire named a terminal that generic surface does not declare — 51 example-corpus-contract violations, one cause. Files present is not the same as a kind registered. Measured against 7b7f3b5: cpu86 resolves as i8086 with its 40 declared terminals, Circuit.fromJSON reports no netlistError, and the corpus-contract per-terminal check clears. This range is 426 commits over the SOLVER, so RE-DERIVED rather than re-stamped: expected-quantities-hold re-solves every numeric claim against bw-board@7b7f3b5 + bw-circuit-ui@c276c0d and PASSES with no new mismatches and the recorded exceptions unchanged; the provenance re-stamp is exactly one bw-board@ revision line per page, every per-page census count and every prose quantity byte-identical — the solver produces the same numbers across the range. bw-board master CI is green on 7b7f3b5.
